title: The Alka-Seltzer plop-plop jingle with Sammy Davis Jr.
summary: He made swing and rock versions of the Alka-Seltzer theme in New York with Ron Carter, Joe LaBarbera and others for Sammy Davis.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Session players on the hits: "I played on that record"

blocks.x: Um hum. Just to wrap up here, we’ve been going for about an hour. Fascinating stuff. The plop-plop-fizz-fizz, when I saw that in something I read about you I went back and I looked, because I remember that from when I was a kid, with Speedy Alka-Seltzer. Now that morphed into something else with Sammy Davis? Is that correct?

Well there was a man by the name of Tom Dawes who actually wrote the melody. He wrote that theme for the advertising agency. He was in some rock band, I can’t remember. But they had so many different versions of that and when Bayer Corporation bought, they bought Alka-Seltzer, they wanted to reach another market, which would be the African-American market. They didn’t have any exposure in that area. So they figured who’s the most important TV personality, black TV personality, Sammy Davis. He was on Johnny Carson all the time. So they got him to do it. So we had that particular run of thought, which was Sammy Davis Junior.
Doing a swing version of it?

I did. They wanted a Woody Herman type version, swing version and they wanted a rock version. And I did both. I did them in New York. I had Ron Carter on bass. I had my brother Joe on drums. I think it was Harold Danko on piano, because he and Joe had an apartment together. But anyway it was a full orchestra, it was great. And we had a Sammy Davis sound-alike scratch vocal guy and then Sammy was in Las Vegas at Caesar’s so I did everything in New York and we did a scratch-vocal.
